title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Milton Keynes

£30,000 - £35,000

Are you an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity within a supportive and collaborative finance team?

We are recruiting for an Accounts Assistant to join a growing business in Milton Keynes. This is a varied role offering exposure to multiple areas of finance, making it ideal for someone who enjoys working as part of a small team and supporting wider accounting functions.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing the purchase ledger and processing supplier invoices
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving account queries
- Assisting with month-end processes and reporting
- Maintaining accurate financial records and data integrity
- Supporting import/export accounting transactions
- Liaising with suppliers and internal stakeholders
- Assisting with ad hoc finance tasks and projects

About You
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant or Purchase Ledger role
- Strong understanding of accounts payable processes
- Experience using accounting software (Xero advantageous)
- High attention to detail and strong organisational skills
- Excellent communication skills
- A proactive team player who can support across multiple finance functions

Benefits
- Salary of £30,000 - £35,000 depending on experience
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Study support and career development opportunities
- Friendly and supportive working environment
- Excellent long-term progression opportunities

If you're looking for a varied Accounts Assistant position where you can develop your skills and become an integral part of a finance team, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Family Law Paralegals (x2) - Luton
description:
Role: Family Paralegal

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is seeking a motivated and talented Family Paralegal to join our highly regarded Family Department. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your career with one of the UK's leading law firms, recognised by The Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners as a top-tier practice and awarded Law Firm of the Year at both the 2024 LexisNexis Awards and the 2023 Modern Law Awards.

Founded in 1998 and headquartered in the City of London, Duncan Lewis Solicitors is a national, award-winning, paperless law firm with over 500 professionals nationwide. Our ethos is simple: "We give people a voice."

Our Family Department is ranked and recommended by The Legal 500 UK and Chambers & Partners UK for its expertise in family and matrimonial law. Described by The Legal 500 as "superbly reliable", "professional, personable, and very efficient", the team provides expert advice and representation across a wide range of family matters. Our specialists include solicitors accredited under the Law Society's Children Law and Family Law Advanced schemes, ensuring clients receive experienced advocacy and consistent support throughout their case.

The department has extensive experience advising clients in complex and sensitive matters, including divorce, financial settlements, child arrangements, domestic abuse, adoption, child abduction, injunctions, and maintenance disputes. The team also regularly acts for high-net-worth individuals, delivering practical and effective solutions tailored to each client's circumstances.

Joining Duncan Lewis means becoming part of a diverse, supportive and forward-thinking organisation where you will have the opportunity to develop your expertise alongside highly respected family law specialists and make a meaningful difference to the lives of children and families.

Duties and responsibilities

As a Family Law Paralegal, you will play a key role in supporting clients across a broad range of Family matters, assisting children, parents, guardians and family members through complex and often sensitive proceedings while helping to achieve the best possible outcomes for those involved.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Report directly to Department Director
- Professional pro-active approach, strong client care skills and a sensitive and sympathetic understanding of clients' needs
- Assisting with casework including dealing with a range of Family matters (LAA Funded and Private client work) as well as undertaking your own advocacy
- Attending clients, taking instructions and preparing cases
- Dealing with correspondence
- Preparing and managing funding applications to the Legal Aid Agency
- Preparing draft documents including witness statements and processing evidence
- Attending conferences and court
- Maintaining accurate time costing procedures
- Implementing any recommendations made by your supervisor following monthly file reviews ensuring that these are dealt with promptly
- Ensuring compliance with file management.

Experience and qualifications

The successful candidate will demonstrate a genuine interest in Family Law and a commitment to delivering exceptional client service.

Essential requirements include:
- A strong academic background with a Law degree
- Demonstrate passion and legal experience in a broad range of Family Law
- Clear understanding and application of Family Laws
- Excellent legal research, drafting and analytical skills.
- Strong organisational and time management abilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Professional, motivated and client-focused approach.
- Business acumen and the ability to market the Company
- Excellent communications skills to work effectively with all types of people
- Excellent analytical and organisational skills and ability to use own initiative but know when to seek guidance
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office and document management systems.

Benefits

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support your professional development, wellbeing, and work-life balance, including:
- Competitive salary with structured pay review process
- Company pension scheme
- 22 days annual leave, increasing with length of service
- Additional birthday leave
- Occupational sick pay
- Payment of practising certificate and relevant professional membership fees
- Access to extensive e-library resources and training webinars
- Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) and wellbeing support
- Employee referral scheme
- Eye care vouchers
- Enhanced family-friendly benefits
- DBS checks paid by the Company
- Flexible and hybrid working options, including part-time arrangements where appropriate
- Support for solicitor qualification and SQE1 examinations
- Clear career progression opportunities
- Support for industry recognition, awards, and professional profile development
- Company Medical Cash Plan

Subject to eligibility and Company policy.

Company culture

At Duncan Lewis Solicitors, we are passionate about creating an environment where talented professionals can thrive. We are proud of our diverse and inclusive workforce and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees.

Our long-standing Investors in People Gold Standard accreditation reflects our commitment to employee development, while our Lexcel, Cyber Essentials Plus and ISO 27001 certifications demonstrate our dedication to excellence, innovation and security.

We invest heavily in the growth of our people through ongoing training, mentoring, clear progression pathways and opportunities to gain industry recognition. Whether you are looking to deepen your expertise, develop leadership skills or advance your career within a nationally recognised law firm, Duncan Lewis provides the platform to help you succeed.

Join a firm where your expertise is valued, your development is supported, and your work makes a genuine difference to the lives of clients across the UK.

title: Paralegal
description:
Role: Paralegal

Department: Family Law/Child

Salary: £23,000 to £27,000 (DOE)

Location: Luton (Hybrid Working Available)

Type: Permanent - Full Time

Job Function: Family Law (Private & Public Children)

Our Client

This is a well-established Legal 500 firm with a strong Family Law practice advising clients across both private and public law matters. The team is recognised for providing compassionate, practical, and client-focused advice in sensitive family cases, including care proceedings, child arrangements, and other Children Act matters.

The firm offers a supportive and collaborative environment where paralegals work closely with experienced solicitors, gaining valuable hands-on experience and opportunities for career development within family law.

Role Overview

The firm is seeking a Care / Family Paralegal to join its growing Family team.

The successful candidate will support solicitors on a varied caseload covering both private family law and public care proceedings. The role offers excellent exposure to all stages of case progression, including drafting legal documents, preparing court bundles, liaising with clients and third parties, and assisting with court proceedings.

This is an ideal opportunity for an organised and proactive individual looking to build or further develop a career in Family Law within a supportive and professional environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist solicitors in managing private family law and public care proceedings.
- Draft correspondence, witness statements, court applications, and legal documents.
- Prepare and manage electronic court bundles and Court Portal filings.
- Conduct legal research and prepare summaries for fee earners.
- Liaise with clients, barristers, social services, experts, and other third parties.
- Assist with disclosure, evidence gathering, and expert instructions.
- Maintain accurate case files and ensure compliance with internal procedures.
- Record time and assist with billing where required.
- Attend court hearings, client meetings, and conferences alongside solicitors as appropriate.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience within a legal environment, preferably in Family Law.
- Exposure to private family matters and/or public care proceedings is advantageous.
- Excellent drafting, organisational, and communication skills.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Professional and discreet approach when handling confidential information. Proficient in Microsoft Office and legal case management systems.
- Familiarity with Court Portal, bundle preparation software, or legal aid processes is advantageous.
- Law degree, GDL, LPC, SQE, or equivalent legal qualification is desirable but not essential.

Compensation & Benefits
- Opportunity to gain valuable experience within a busy Family Law team.
- Exposure to both private and public family law matters.
- Hybrid working arrangements.
- Ongoing training, mentoring, and career development opportunities.
- Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including enhanced annual leave and birthday leave after one year of service.

title: Underwriting Support Administrator
description:
Underwriting Support Administrator

Our client, a well-established financial mutual, is seeking a Underwriting Support Administratorto join their Operations team, reporting to the Operations Director. The role is responsible for collecting and processing medical and lifestyle information to generate one-off premiums for client care plans, preparing and sending quotes to Financial Advisers, processing applications, and providing ongoing administrative support for active plans.

This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-focused administrator from an insurance, financial services or care background who is confident handling sensitive information and enjoys varied, relationship-led work across advisers, clients and their families.

Key Responsibilities:
- Gather and verify medical, lifestyle and personal information to calculate one-off care plan premiums
- Input data into underwriting and premium calculation tools to generate accurate quotes
- Send quotes to Financial Advisers and respond promptly to queries
- Review completed acceptances for accuracy, following up on any outstanding information
- Maintain accurate records for active plans, including amendments, updates and annual existence checks
- Process death notifications sensitively, verifying documentation and updating records and payments accordingly
- Liaise with family representatives, care providers, Financial Advisers and internal teams
- Work closely with finance to ensure accurate billing, payments and record management
- Act as the main administrative point of contact for Financial Advisers, clients and their families

Requirements
- Strong administrative experience within insurance, financial services or a care setting
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Confident written and verbal communicator, able to convey information clearly to a range of audiences
- Comfortable handling sensitive medical and financial information confidentially
- Understanding of data protection and compliance requirements
- Proficient with IT systems and Microsoft Office
- Experience in underwriting administration or insurance quoting, or knowledge of care plans, is desirable

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a supportive, fully remote team, working across a varied and genuinely meaningful role that supports members and their families at important moments.

title: Faculty Support Administrator
description:
Faculty or Department: Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences
Based at: Cranfield Campus, Cranfield, Bedfordshire
Hours of work: 37 hours per week, normally worked Monday to Friday. Flexible working will be considered.
Contract type: Permanent
Salary: Full time starting salary is normally in the range of £27,537 per annum
Apply by: 04/10/2026

Role Description

We welcome highly organised, self-motivated people to join our team to provide administration support with things including, but not limited to, raising orders for equipment and booking travel requests.

About the Role

You will need to provide first-class administrative support as part of a pooled resource to academic staff, research staff and PhD researchers within the Centres/Theme, which will include processing purchase orders, booking travel, managing emails and general enquiries, coordinating internal and external meetings, conferences and seminars, and maintaining up-to-date records on internal databases. This role ensures operational efficiency, professionalism and high standards of customer service, while proactively recommending improvements where appropriate.

The role is a key part of a flexible 'pooled resource' at the thematic level, coordinated by the Personal Assistant to the Director of Theme. Operating as a shared resource, the role will support major initiatives across the Theme and, where necessary, as directed by business needs and the Administration Team Lead, provide cover for the Faculty Administration Team and provide Faculty- and University-wide support.

About You

Maintaining effective relationships is key to the job. You will therefore need to be able to demonstrate excellent interpersonal skills, including written and verbal communication skills, as you will be communicating with a wide network of staff and students within the Theme. You will be privy to confidential information in relation to staff, students and business decisions, and it is imperative that absolute discretion and confidentiality is shown, whilst contributing to the sense of professionalism with external contacts/clients and promoting the values of the organisation.

Using your experience in administrative work, you will have a thorough understanding of office systems, processes and databases, and a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office packages such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Access.

You must have the ability to manage workload independently but also support the wider team and have knowledge and initiative to resolve both standard and non-standard issues and queries, being proactive and taking the initiative to manage issues and find solutions promptly to ensure smooth and effective administrative support. You will be able to refer to the team for guidance as appropriate. The ability to prioritise and organise effectively a disparate range of tasks with minimal supervision, and the ability to work under pressure whilst maintaining attention to detail and accuracy, are important aspects of the role.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield's world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here .

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here .

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families . Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here .

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

How to apply

For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Sasha Quill, Administration Team Lead and Personal Assistant to the Director of Theme, on (E):

Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on (E): . Please quote reference number 5393.

Closing date for receipt of applications: 4 October 2026

title: Receptionist
description: Do you have a friendly voice, a calm manner, and a passion for helping people? At Sharnbrook Surgery, our reception team is the first point of contact for our patients - they are that reassuring voice on the other end of the phone and the welcoming smile at the desk. Are you dependable, organised and able to juggle multiple tasks whilst remaining calm even on the busiest of days? Do you want to work for a close-knit, multidisciplinary team who support each other through the busy days and celebrate the wins together. An organisation who values open communication, flexible working, and a healthy work-life balance? Well this is what it is like to work for Sharnbrook Surgery! If you are reading this and think, this is me! This is the kind of organisation I would like to work for! Then we would welcome your application for the role of Receptionist. There is one part-time vacancy for 20hours per week. The working days are to be confirmed, however, please note that the successful candidate will be required to over 3 days, one 0800-1700, one 0930-1830 and one 1200-1600 per week. The successful candidate will demonstrate an ability to be flexible to do additional hours if required and offer flexibility for swaps etc. to support the needs of the service. Interviews will be held on Wednesday 21st October 2026. As Receptionist you will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a friendly, professional welcome both in person and over the phone. You will play a vital role in ensuring the smooth running of the practice through carrying out a wide range of administration duties including, but not limited to booking patient appointments, opening post, scanning health records, processing the registration of new patients and supporting both clinical and non-clinical colleagues. The role offers variety and opportunities to enhance existing skills and learn new ones. No two days will ever be the same. Primary Responsibilities The following are the core responsibilities of the Receptionist. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system i.e. make / cancel / rearrange appointments via the clinical system Processing of new and temporary registrations, patient discharges and all associated patient information as required ensuring accuracy and timely completion. Scan patient medical records, results and letters as required. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately. Signpost and support patients to the correct services as advised and/or as per pre-determined pathways. Ensure patient information is always up to date and accurate. Greet patients and visitors arriving at the reception desk, ensuring they have checked in. As appropriate ensure support is required in these tasks. Observe patients and visitors in the waiting room and alert an appropriate member of staff to any concerns or issues. This includes any wellbeing and security concerns. Ensure the waiting and reception areas are kept tidy and that information displayed is up to date. Updating noticeboards with regular health promotions. Ensure effective communications, regularly updating the Team Leader of any issues. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies. Always ensure confidentiality and professionalism with patients, visitors and colleagues. Assist in maintaining the safety of staff, patients and visitors. Always maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area, ensuring compliance with the Surgerys clear desk policy at the end of each working day. This includes wiping down workstation to maintain infection, prevention and control standards. Carry out any other duties as reasonably requested by colleagues. Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient and timely manner. Support colleagues throughout the surgery with general tasks as requested and appropriate Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to: Partake in audit as directed. Provide cross cover during planned and unplanned absences. Arrange and take minutes at meetings as required and appropriate. Raise orders for surgery consumables such as toners, hand towels etc. as instructed and required. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota. Support the OM with regular premises checks such as fire alarm testing and water testing as required.
